# `glue`

the two hemispheres of a cortex glued by a bridge, a derived manifold stored with its map to the original and its bridge selection.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run glue --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run glue --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run glue --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex_pial
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `surface` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$surface"} (name the two-hemisphere surface (--surface)) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `surface` | `--surface` | none | - |  | the two-hemisphere surface, by name |
| `name` | `--name` | `{surface}_glued` | - |  | the glued surface's name |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`geometry.glue`](../nodes.md) | surface=surface |  | glued, map, bridge |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `glued` | kind manifold, type surface, name $name, derived_from surface.manifold.0 |
| `map` | kind field, kind_name glue map, name {name}_map, on glued |
| `bridge` | kind selection, type indices, name {name}_bridge, on glued |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE GLUED CORTEX: the two hemispheres joined by the corpus callosum's bridge, a DERIVED manifold made by its own definition (a `make` move). The imported two-hemisphere mesh stays the manifold of
record (atlases, kernels, exports, results, figures); the glued surface is the default COMPUTATIONAL manifold for spatiotemporal pattern analysis (patterns cross hemispheres smoothly: one cortex), and results are
reported back on the original two hemispheres.

The definition stores the glued surface with its MAP (glued vertex -> original vertex, -1 on the bridge) and the BRIDGE as a labelled irregular selection ("bridge: not cortex"). Transfers: original -> glued (values
kept copied; the bridge by sourcesOf interpolation; the medial wall has no counterpart) and glued -> original (exact; the bridge dropped like the medial wall); atlases are carried by `transfer`. Orientations are also
reported in the anatomical frame (canonical frames, gauge recorded) as a check on the bridge's transport. `eigenmodes` and `apply_kernel` take this surface BY NAME: a flag that only chooses the input (`--glued`) is gone.

What it cannot resolve: the pieces must match by anatomy (the medial walls cut, a bridge grown); a pair that does not match is refused with the reason.

  nxr-neuro run glue --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex_pial
```
